title: Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet (Paris AI Action Summit)
issuer: French Presidency of the AI Action Summit and participating States
reason: Official Élysée page and PDF read. The statement is a non-binding political declaration adopted on 11 February 2025; the official page lists 65 endorsers (63 States, the EU and the African Union Commission), while the PDF lists 64 and a contemporaneous Canadian release listed 60. The discrepancy is recorded in the instrument record.
evidence: Official Élysée English page, official 3-page PDF (SHA-256 9a19a426c0d1ffdcd2dab40340074663ca4e8ff3eaeb1c3d1d2067e3fd9a2c64), and the Government of Canada's contemporaneous release.
gaps: Endorser list inconsistent across official publications (60/64/65); no depositary or update log; US and UK did not endorse.

title: Global AI Governance Initiative
issuer: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
reason: Official MFA English text and Chinese original located. A unilateral Chinese government proposal for international AI governance, issued on 18 October 2023; non-binding and with no formal adherence list. It is the principal documented Chinese-pole instrument and is included as a non-binding principles document, not as an agreed international instrument.
evidence: Official MFA English text (stored HTML, SHA-256 073933c76fa44d0cf1f30d1cbe95b17ad6a625f29abd12024e3550f2adde5b59) and the Cyberspace Administration of China original.
gaps: No endorsement list; the 2025 Global AI Governance Action Plan is not separately catalogued; only the English translation is stored.

title: Collaboration on the safety of AI: UK-US memorandum of understanding
reason: Official GOV.UK publication and press release read. Bilateral MOU signed on 1 April 2024 by Michelle Donelan and Gina Raimondo; non-binding; implemented by the UK and US AI Safety Institutes. GOV.UK publishes a summary of key elements, not the full MOU, so the record is metadata-only.
evidence: Official GOV.UK publication (2 April 2024) and press release; signature by the UK Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology and the US Secretary of Commerce; no full MOU text linked.
gaps: Full MOU text not published; the summary states no duration, termination, review or dispute-settlement procedure.

title: Joint Statement EU-US Trade and Technology Council of 4-5 April 2024 (AI Safety Dialogue commitment)
reason: Official European Commission and USTR joint statement read. The AI section records a commitment by the European AI Office and the US AI Safety Institute to establish a Dialogue; it is a political commitment in a broader joint statement, not a standalone MOU, administrative arrangement or binding agreement.
evidence: European Commission and USTR joint statement, 5 April 2024; NIST and European Commission pages on the first technical Dialogue, 11 July 2024; no standalone terms of reference located.
gaps: No standalone US–EU AI-safety MOU or administrative arrangement located; the commitment creates no binding obligations.

title: International AI Safety Report
issuer: International expert panel chaired by Yoshua Bengio, commissioned by the AI Seoul Summit
reason: Authoritative international scientific report, not an instrument creating obligations. It is a candidate for the 'authoritative materials' layer, but its 2025 and later editions were not verified on an official source in this session.
evidence: Discovery only.
gaps: Official publication URL, date and editions need verification.

title: CCW Group of Governmental Experts on Emerging Technologies in the Area of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
issuer: UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons
reason: The principal multilateral military-AI negotiating track. Its 2024–2026 final report (CCW/GGE.1/2026/3, adopted 4 September 2026) sets out elements of an instrument and other measures. The Seventh Review Conference endorsed them and continued the GGE with a mandate to elaborate an instrument, without prejudging its nature, and to recommend its legal form, including a binding protocol.
evidence: Official UNODA GGE meeting page, final report CCW/GGE.1/2026/3, and the Seventh Review Conference final document CCW/CONF.VII/CRP.1/Rev.3 (20 November 2026) read.
gaps: No adopted instrument or draft protocol; the 2026 report is not a treaty text. First 2027 sessions scheduled 1–5 March and 30 August–3 September 2027.
